content.title: Irrigation Ditches
content.summary: Irrigation ditches in the Denver metro area, including Arvada, were established in the 1860s to transport water for agricultural use and now serve various users. Over 60 ditches run through Arvada, with the Farmers' High Line Canal, Croke Canal, and Church Ditch being the largest. Maintenance responsibilities lie primarily with the ditch companies, and residents must coordinate with these companies for any work near the ditches, as the city does not perform maintenance in those areas.
content.body:
Irrigation canals wind through the Denver metro area, including the City of Arvada. Many of the ditches were constructed in the 1860s, including the Farmers' High Line Canal (FHL), Croke Canal and the Church Ditch. Urban / suburban areas have developed around the ditches. Since the ditch water runs seasonally, not everyone realizes their purpose and importance.

### [Irrigation Canals FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=41)

[What are irrigation ditches?](#)
:   Irrigation ditches were originally built as early as the 1860’s to convey water rights to farms and ranches. Now irrigation ditches deliver water for a variety of users. Most ditches run water from April through October with some that run water year-round to fill reservoirs.

[Where are the irrigation ditches in Arvada?](#)
:   There are over 60 irrigation ditches that run through Arvada in nearly every part of the city. Three of the largest ditches include:

    - Farmers’ Highline Canal
    - Croke Canal
    - Church Ditch

    The [Arvada Ditch Map](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JgLgW7fllooSJdT4-fgpEp-uR2gEQkIm/view?usp=sharing) shows all of the ditches in Arvada. Google Maps also has some ditches mapped and labeled.

[Who owns irrigation ditches?](#)
:   Ditches are owned collectively by shareholders who are typically part of an incorporated ditch company. The shareholders often include a mix of individuals, farms, municipalities, governmental agencies or industrial users.

[Who owns the property where the ditch is located?](#)
:   A ditch company rarely owns the land on which it is located. More often, ditches go through property owned by others. The ditch company typically holds a prescriptive easement allowing the ditch company access to the property for the delivery of water and ditch maintenance without needing permission. Some ditch easements are recorded but a majority are prescriptive and are not included on development plats.

[Who is responsible for maintenance near an irrigation ditch?](#)
:   The ditch company is only responsible for maintaining the ditch for water deliveries. Performing work in the ditch easement must be coordinated with the ditch company and underlying property owner. You may contact a ditch company directly to see if they will allow or are willing to partner on maintenance for aesthetics, debris removal, fire mitigation, or any other purpose.

    \*See FAQ about how to contact ditch companies.

[Can the City perform maintenance near the irrigation ditch by my house?](#)
:   The City does not complete maintenance along irrigation ditches. Residents interested in completing fire mitigation or other maintenance along ditches must obtain permission from and coordinate with the ditch company and underlying property owner.

    \*See FAQ about how to contact ditch companies.

[How can I contact the ditch company?](#)
:   Contact information for the main three ditches in Arvada is available on the City’s [irrigation ditches webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/512/Irrigation-Canals). Other ditch companies may have websites or contact information online.

    If you cannot find information online, please reach out to the City through [Ask Arvada](http://arvadaco.gov/898) and a team member will try to assist you.

[Can I throw yard waste or other trash in the ditch?](#)
:   Please do not throw anything in the ditches, even grass clippings and especially dog poop. Ditches are a vital water source, and you or someone downstream may use this water for irrigation or drinking after treatment. Additionally, yard waste left piled on the ditch banks can cause erosion problems.

[I have a ditch in my yard. Can I use the water?](#)
:   No, not unless you have purchased shares in that ditch company and are a recognized shareholder. Using the water without owning shares is considered water theft.

[How are irrigation ditches different than stormwater ditches?](#)
:   Stormwater ditches receive storm runoff from your neighborhood and direct the water to the nearest natural stream, such as Little Dry Creek or Ralston Creek. Irrigation ditches run seasonally to provide water for irrigation.
